verdicts.note: Incumbent treasurer since 2019 with nearly 34 years of county service (S1). S2 independently confirms her as the current officeholder. That is a maximal record case, and high confidence holds.
He calls himself 'a political outsider' (S1), has no office record, and qualified as a write-in (S2). +2 high holds.

The platform centers on scrutiny: 'the financial discipline to review and challenge how public money is handled' and 'eliminating fraud ... by thoroughly reviewing and scrutinizing transactions' (S1). That is the oversight/audit pole. The slate blurb on his own site (S4) adds that he founded a group 'dedicated to government accountability,' which reinforces the reading. -1 medium is appropriate because he states no position on spending levels.

notes: Considered and rejected spending for Brunson. 'Manage county resources with integrity, accountability, and fiscal responsibility' and 'reduced banking costs' (S1) are administrative claims about running the office, not a stated restraint-versus-investment position. No taxes evidence for either candidate: the treasurer collects taxes but does not set them, and neither candidate states a position on tax levels or I-645.
